ci-bot: CI perf alert: dedicated-runner-42 observed 18% p50 increase and 2 OOMs on longctx benchmark (job=9876) at 2026-07-13T14:02:01Z. failing test: perf/long-seqlen/bench.sh :eyes:
jia: link to logs?
ci-bot: https://ci.redwood.local/job/9876/console - OOMs in worker-3, attach: /artifacts/9876/oom-logs.tgz
omar: saw this in staging last night too. reproducer: `./bench --model=gptx --seq-len=8192 --concurrency=4` -> worker hits OOM after ~2200 requests.
marina: interesting — the OOMs look like KV-cache memory growth + slab swap. can someone run `pmap` and `smem` on the process when repro hits OOM?
luc: ran a local repro, grabbing snippet:```
# top few lines before OOM
PID   USER   RSS   VSZ  %MEM COMMAND
3124  svc    9.8G  12G  7.6  redwood-runtime --config /etc/rr/config
# dmesg
Out of memory: Killed process 3124 (redwood-runtime) total-vm:12500000kB, anon-rss:9800000kB, file-rss:200000kB
```
omar: thanks — also saw high majflt count in `perf stat`: majflt ~ 120k over the run. suggests heavy page-in from swap or mmap churn.
marina: bisect timeline: regression first landed around merge window for PR #4321 (kernel-selection + kv eviction refactor). luc, you authored the eviction change right?
luc: yeah that was me. PR description: "kv: introduce stride-based compaction + eviction window to reduce fragmentation for tiny tokens". I changed the eviction loop to scan stride-aligned slabs rather than strict LRU. assumption was less fragmentation, better throughput. 
jia: can you run a bisect with the repro between commit `a1b2c3d` (pre-change) and `d4e5f6g` (post-change)? we need minimal blame.
luc: did quick bisection locally: commit `c7f8e9a` is the first bad. diff highlights:`
--- a/kv/cache.cpp
+++ b/kv/cache.cpp
@@
- // old: strict lru walk
- for (auto &entry: lru_list) { try_evict(entry); }
+ // new: stride compaction to avoid chasing small-lived entries
+ for (int i = 0; i < slabs_count; i += stride) { compact_slab(i); }
`
omar: that matches what I saw. stride compaction reduces bookkeeping but it looks like it skips seq-length locality: long requests build big contiguous KV ranges and the stride skip prevents timely eviction => huge resident set.
patrick: any perf/prof evidence? flamegraph or heap profile?
luc: attached pprof snapshot: heap growth correlates with longctx requests. flame: `kv_alloc()` hot during long sequences. also traced `kv_cache->compact_slab()` taking 40ms on hot path.
marina: hypothesis: stride compaction reduces CPU overhead normally, but for long sequence distributions it delays eviction of contiguous KV blocks; combined with kernel selection changes that increased kernel pinning, we see pages staying resident -> major page faults when memory pressure forces swap.
jia: can we validate by toggling stride? is there an env flag to restore old LRU path?
luc: added `KV_EVICT_STRIDE=0` in debug build which forces the old LRU walker. quick canary: with stride=0 the repro completed 10k requests w/o OOM, p50 restored to baseline. with stride=8 (the default) it OOMs.
patrick: ok this is a rollout blocker. plan: revert eviction heuristic in runtime branch until we design a sequence-length aware compactor. I'd prefer a quick revert PR and a canary deploy.
marina: +1. Also add a CI long-seqlen test to catch this going forward.
sre-bot: Incident logged: INF-2026-074; severity=high; affected: dedicated & private staging clusters. owner=eng-runtime.
jia: luc — can you open revert PR against main and add the env toggle as a short-term guard? mention the exact commit `c7f8e9a` in the PR text. include repro steps and perf artifacts.
luc: on it. I'll do revert + feature flag in a single PR so we can re-enable later. PR draft soon.
omar: after revert, can we run an extended soak (48h) with seq-len=8192 workload to be safe?
patrick: schedule soak on canary pool, gate rollout on zero OOMs and p50 within 5% of baseline.
jia: one more ask: add a small perf test in CI that runs `bench --seq-len=4096/8192` at low qps to catch page-fault regressions (doesn't need to be fast, can be tagged perf-long).
marina: logging items for follow-ups: - design compactor aware of token-range cardinality - consider async compaction off hot path - kernel selection: avoid pinning suspects under heavy mem pressure - add eviction metrics (evicted_bytes, compaction_time)
luc: opened PR #4387 (revert + toggle) and added repro and `pprof` snapshot links. pinging when CI green. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: PR #4387 CI: started (job 9901).
jenkins: canary deploy scheduled to pool `canary-evict-fix` after CI pass.
marina: thanks team. will follow up with postmortem (short) and add perf-long CI job.
jia: moving this to rollout-blocker and assigning to eng-runtime on tracker. if anyone notices other regressions, drop quick notes here. :pray:
